items.title: Encrypted off-device backup + restore drill
items.why: Persistence and generations do not recover a lost SSD or deleted documents.
items.next: Inventory existing backups; choose destination, quota, recovery credentials and retention before configuring Restic.
items.acceptance: Restore documents, a password database and independent age/LUKS recovery material without relying on this laptop.
items.risk: Recurring storage cost, sensitive key material and accidental overwrite during restore.

items.title: Repeatable battery baseline
items.why: There is no universal best power daemon; the screen and workloads may dominate.
items.next: Compare balanced/power-saver and advertised 60/120 Hz modes with fixed brightness and workload. Record watts and task energy.
items.acceptance: Repeat measurements, retain responsiveness, verify GPU sleep and restore the original profile/mode.
items.risk: One instantaneous sample is not a battery benchmark; do not stack tuning daemons.

items.title: GPU sleep and suspend/resume acceptance
items.why: RTD3 was observed working, but external displays, games and resume can change it.
items.next: Check both GPU PCI functions after offload/monitor disconnect. Test lock, resume, Wi-Fi/audio and overnight unplugged drain.
items.acceptance: No lost session, correct lock, repeatable drain and return to runtime suspension after workloads finish.
items.risk: Save work; unsupported deep sleep or hibernation must not be forced.

items.status: State declared; migration and host checks pending
items.title: Scrub/SMART alerts and ephemeral state
items.why: Scrub and SMART already exist; scheduling is not proof of completed work or delivered warnings.
items.next: Migrate existing Btrfs, SMART and PPD state before activating the new mounts. Verify completed scrub history, missed timers, selected-profile survival and smartd notification delivery.
items.acceptance: An alert reaches you, a scrub completes, the selected profile and relevant history survive reboot, and the new mounts are verified.
items.risk: An empty new mount can hide existing state; background I/O costs battery and single-device scrub cannot repair every corruption.

items.title: Reviewed updates and known-good retention
items.why: Latest kernel + latest NVIDIA driver + unstable creates a large regression surface.
items.next: Adopt weekly review/security updates, targeted input bumps and post-reboot checks. Inspect cleanup retention before deleting generations.
items.acceptance: Build/test/boot checklist passes and a known-good boot generation remains reachable.
items.risk: Neither stale pins nor frequent unreviewed updates are safe; Flatpaks update independently.

items.status: First isolation pass; host acceptance pending
items.title: Review actual session and network protections
items.why: AppArmor enablement is not profile coverage; a VPN icon is not a routing test.
items.next: Activate the reviewed account and Flatpak changes; use a fresh login to verify device access, file portals and calls. After retiring the managed-agent policy, restart the desktop app and verify Git reads and approved development commands with its built-in sandbox. Then inspect AppArmor coverage, reproduce the PAM workaround and verify VPN IPv4/IPv6/DNS.
items.acceptance: Document effective protections and necessary exceptions with a reproducible removal test.
items.risk: Authentication, DNS and USB policy changes can lock you out or break connectivity.

items.title: Evaluate Lanzaboote Secure Boot
items.why: Disk encryption does not establish boot-artifact integrity.
items.owner: Future host-selected boot module + persistent signing keys
items.next: Verify firmware recovery, vendor keys, ESP capacity and external credentials; build signed artifacts before considering enrollment.
items.acceptance: Verified recovery, signed boot, functional NVIDIA/OpenRazer, boot rollback and protected independent PKI backup.
items.risk: Firmware mistakes can prevent boot. TPM unlock is a separate threat-model decision.

items.title: Consider TuneD or TLP only for a measured gap
items.why: Modern alternatives offer extra policy controls, not a guaranteed battery improvement.
items.next: Check locked Nixpkgs integration and shell compatibility, then trial ONE backend with rollback to PPD.
items.acceptance: Repeatable energy benefit without resume, USB, audio, Wi-Fi or responsiveness regressions.
items.risk: Backend/API compatibility and conflicting device policies; don't change for novelty alone.

items.title: Review Signal database-key storage
items.why: The installed Flatpak defaults to basic plaintext database-key storage; its launcher warns encrypted backends can cause data loss.
items.next: Back up the closed Signal profile and keyring to protected persistent storage, rehearse gnome-libsecret migration separately and verify two launches plus a reboot before changing the live backend.
items.acceptance: Existing messages remain readable across two launches and reboot, the key uses the intended keyring, and an independently usable rollback is retained.
items.risk: Changing backend without a working keyring can make the message database unreadable; do not delete or reset the profile.
